source.check: candidates, full names and labels from the News-Letter's complete list of nominations (6 May; * = retiring member as printed there) and its report of withdrawals (8 May); the Duncairn votes, majority, spoiled papers and electorate from the News-Letter's results text, the majority equal to the difference of the printed votes

note: Annual election of one councillor in each of the 15 wards of Belfast Corporation (the 1936 cohort) and the triennial election of seven aldermen (Duncairn, Ormeau, Pottinger, Smithfield, St Anne's, St George's, Woodvale); nominations Friday 5 May, poll Monday 15 May 1939. Sixteen of the 22 seats were filled unopposed at nomination; after four withdrawals on 6 May the Duncairn aldermanship was the only contest in Belfast (Belfast News-Letter, 6, 8 and 16 May 1939). Neill, a councillor for the ward, was the official Unionist nominee for the aldermanship vacated by James M'Kinney, who resigned; labels from the list of nominations (6 May). Small poll. Polled Monday 15 May 1939: the Duncairn result was announced at the City Hall at 10.30 the night before the Belfast News-Letter and the Irish News of 16 May 1939 (both p. 7) reported it. The Belfast Corporation register of members (PRONI LA/7/1/CA/1/3) heads this round 16 May 1939, the day after.
